mutations.why: The whole point of routing profile-block's write path through upsertBlock is that the refusal now names the span it collided with. Dropping the marker names restores the old ambiguous wording in a document that can hold more than one kind of span - and no assertion outside this sprint's would notice, because nothing else ever asserted on this message.
mutations.label: marker-block:unterminated-names-marker
mutations.expectRed: must name the marker it collided with

mutations.why: The exit code is the only thing a /checkpoint gate reads. Pinning it to zero is precisely the failure mutate.js exists to prevent - a manifest whose anchors have rotted waved through as evidence - and before this sprint no test could reach the decision at all.
mutations.label: mutate:cli-exit-code
mutations.expectRed: a run that is not evidence must exit non-zero

mutations.why: --json exists so another tool can parse the run. Falling through to the text branch emits a table ahead of the JSON, which a parser sees as malformed input; nothing else in the suite reads the render branch.
mutations.label: mutate:cli-json-only
mutations.expectRed: no text or markdown alongside the JSON

mutations.why: A throw that reports before it reverts leaves a mutated file on disk looking like the author's own edit. restoreInFlight is what stops that, and the runCli path to it was untested until this sprint.
mutations.label: mutate:cli-restore-before-report
mutations.expectRed: a throw must revert before it reports
